title: The Unread Appointment Text
story: In May the clinic stopped printing appointment slips and sent text reminders instead. Most patients adapted without trouble. Okonkwo did not, because his handset stayed in a drawer and he still expected a card. He missed a blood-pressure review and learned of it only when a nurse rang to ask why the chair was empty. The system had marked the reminder delivered, which meant the network had received it, not that he had read it. Nurse Adewale recorded a contact problem rather than a failure to attend. She booked a fresh slot by telephone and had him write the time on a kitchen calendar. She added a file note: do not rely on text alone. A delivered message, for him, was not a message that had been seen. The file note stopped that difference from being mistaken for indifference.

vocabulary.definition: Changed habits to fit a new system.
Received by the network, whether or not it was read.
A planned check of a health condition.

quiz.question: How did Okonkwo find out that he had missed the review?
options: A nurse rang to ask about the empty chair
A printed slip arrived the next morning
His handset lit up inside the drawer
A notice was pinned to his front door
quiz.correctAnswer: A nurse rang to ask about the empty chair
quiz.explanation: He learned of the miss only when a nurse rang to ask why the chair was empty.
quiz.supportingSentence: He missed a blood-pressure review and learned of it only when a nurse rang to ask why the chair was empty.

quiz.question: What instruction did Adewale add to his file?
options: Do not rely on text alone
Cancel every future health check
Charge a fee for an empty chair
Stop all messages to every patient
quiz.correctAnswer: Do not rely on text alone
quiz.explanation: She added a file note saying not to rely on text alone.
quiz.supportingSentence: She added a file note: do not rely on text alone.

quiz.question: What wrong conclusion did the file note prevent?
options: That he missed the visit because he did not care
That the clinic had closed its doors in May
That printed slips had been made illegal
That the nurse had removed his handset
quiz.correctAnswer: That he missed the visit because he did not care
quiz.explanation: The note stops the gap between a sent text and a seen text from being mistaken for indifference.
quiz.supportingSentence: The file note stopped that difference from being mistaken for indifference.

quiz.question: What does delivered mean about the reminder in this passage?
options: Accepted by the phone network
Read out loud by the patient
Printed on a card and posted
Copied by hand onto a calendar
quiz.explanation: Marked delivered meant the network had received the reminder, not that Okonkwo had read it.
quiz.supportingSentence: The system had marked the reminder delivered, which meant the network had received it, not that he had read it.

quiz.question: Why does the writer say that most patients adapted?
options: To show the new messages worked for many people
To prove paper slips had never been used
To blame Okonkwo for building the system
To claim every patient stored a phone in a drawer
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the new messages worked for many people
quiz.explanation: Most patients adapted without trouble, so the failure is particular to Okonkwo rather than universal.
